text:
maya: Heads-up — saw two spot GPU evictions in us-west2 during the 03:00 window that triggered stream token failures for demo-svc. Clients saw stalled streams and then hard reconnects, which caused duplicate partial responses.

sam: Ugh. Do we have a reproducible trace? logs showed vm preempted, runtime attempted graceful drain but stream cutoff before token sync finished.

maya: Putting the small trace here: `runtime: drain start -> flush tokens -> attempt cutover -> kill` — cutover step sometimes times out if the new pod takes >2s to accept the stream token.

anil: What cutover mode are we using? full-token-migrate or token-bridge?

maya: Right now it's token-migrate (we try to push KV to target and transfer ownership). That requires fast warm start on the target. If the target is delayed, sender abandons.

claire: Suggest we experiment with a hybrid: requeue incoming requests to a short-lived spillover queue while token-bridge does background sync, then resume streaming from a fresh session.

sam: Agreed. Two levers: 1) increase drain_grace to tolerate slower cold starts, 2) introduce requeue+spillover to avoid client-side dupes. But longer grace = longer capacity hold on preemptible GPUs. Cost tradeoff.

leo: Proposal sketch: keep drain_grace low (1.5s), enable fast in-memory token-bridge on same AZ + a tiny requeue window (500ms) where requests are buffered and either resumed or reissued. That keeps hold time small and limits duplicated outputs.

maya: Example config I prototyped: 
```
preemptible_handling:
  drain_grace_ms: 1500
  requeue_window_ms: 500
  bridge_mode: optimistic
  bridge_backoff_ms: 50
```

sam: Nice. "optimistic" bridge_mode = send token snapshots to eligible targets immediately and let the target accept if it warms in time, otherwise the requeue kicks in?

anil: Exactly. Also need idempotency tokens on client-level requests to de-dupe. Add header `X-Req-Id` and make runtime check before emitting second partials.

claire: We should also measure the failure tail for cold starts when target pinned to cheaper families (A100 vs T4). If warm-up latency > requeue_window we either need to widen the window or pick warmer pool for quick cutover.

leo: Can do a small perf sweep: 1000 simulated cutovers across GPU families and record median/95/99 cold start times. Use those to set per-pool requeue_window defaults.

maya: Also saw network flakiness between zones. For cross-zone cutovers we should not attempt token-migrate; fall back to requeue only. Bridge only intra-zone.

sam: Good call. Add routing policy: if target_region != source_region -> disable bridge, enable requeue with increased window. Something like: `cutover_policy: { intra_zone: bridge+requeue(500ms), cross_zone: requeue(1500ms) }`.

deploy-bot: Deploy request queued: canary preemptible-handler-v2 -> eng-runtime/staging (kickoff).

claire: For rollout: start with canary on staging then 5% traffic in us-west2 only. Monitor stream-drop metric and partial-dupe-rate. Alert thresholds: drop_rate > 0.5% or dupes > 0.2% -> rollback.

anil: Added checklist: update SDK to send X-Req-Id, runtime to check idempotency, enable per-pool defaults, cross-zone disable bridge.

maya: Also note billing/cost: if bridge fails often and we widen drain_grace, preemptible cost benefit reduces. We should add a metric to estimate extra GPU-seconds caused by extended_grace and surface in console per-customer.

leo: I'll wire up a short job to estimate extra seconds per eviction given drain_grace. That will let product choose between strict cost vs smoother UX.

sam: One last item: test plan for race where client reconnects to a different instance and tries to resume with stale token. Need strict token TTL and a short revocation window. If token mismatch, runtime should return `HTTP 409 resume_conflict` with hint to requeue.

maya: OK next steps: (1) run perf sweep (leo), (2) implement bridge+requeue prototype (sam + anil), (3) SDK idempotency header update (claire), (4) canary deploy in us-west2 (deploy-bot). I'll own the rollout checklist.

claire: Thanks — ping me when canary started, I'll watch alerts. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll open a short RFC with the config knobs and simulation results.

maya: Thanks team — let's aim to have canary by EOD tomorrow.

leo: noted, will post results in this thread when the sweep finishes.

deploy-bot: Canary started: preemptible-handler-v2 -> us-west2 5% traffic.

maya: Closing the loop later with metrics.
